Let \(L_k=\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\ldots,k)\).  
For \(m=\lfloor \sqrt[3]{n}\rfloor\):

- If \(n=m^3\), we need \(L_{m-1}\mid m^3\).
- If \(m^3<n<(m+1)^3\), we need \(L_m\mid n\).

For \(m=1,\dots,7\), the largest possible \(n\) in each interval is:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
m & L_m & \text{largest working } n \text{ for this } m\\
\hline
1 & 1 & 7\\
2 & 2 & 26\\
3 & 6 & 60\\
4 & 12 & 120\\
5 & 60 & 180\\
6 & 60 & 300\\
7 & 420 & 420
\end{array}
\]

For \(m\ge 8\), \(L_m>(m+1)^3\). Indeed, this is checked directly for \(8\le m\le 14\), and for \(m\ge 15\),
\[
L_m\ge 2^{m-1}>(m+1)^3.
\]
Thus no non-cube \(n\) with \(m\ge 8\) works. Also, for \(m=8\), \(L_7=420\nmid 512\), and for \(m\ge 9\), \(L_{m-1}>m^3\), so no perfect cube works either.

Therefore the largest such integer is \(\boxed{420}\).
